review.summary: This PR deprecates `falcon.testing.redirected` in favor of the stdlib `contextlib.redirect_stdout`/`redirect_stderr`. The change is small, well-scoped, and follows the project's established deprecation pattern (decorator, news fragment, docstring directive, removal scheduled for 5.0). The internal callers have been migrated and a deprecation-warning test was added. No correctness issues are evident; the only items worth flagging are a documentation typo ("stlib") and a couple of minor stylistic/scope considerations.

issues.detail: The `.. deprecated:: 4.3` directive in `falcon/testing/helpers.py` reads "Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`...". This should be "stdlib's". Minor, but it will render verbatim in the published docs.

issues.description: Deprecation message could point users at the exact replacement idiom
issues.detail: The runtime warning text says "Please use contextlib.redirect_stdout and contextlib.redirect_stderr instead." That is accurate but does not mention that the two stdlib managers must be nested (or stacked via `ExitStack`) to replicate the dual stdout+stderr redirection that `redirected(stdout=..., stderr=...)` offers in a single `with` statement. A one-line hint in the docstring would prevent a foreseeable migration footgun.

issues.description: Test does not assert deprecation fires exactly once / does not exercise stderr path
issues.detail: `test_deprecated_redirected` in `tests/test_testing.py` only covers the `stdout` redirection path and relies on `pytest.warns` (which passes if at least one matching warning fires). Given the function takes both `stdout` and `stderr`, a second case (or parametrization) covering `stderr=...` would mirror the migration the PR is asking users to perform and protect against a future regression in either branch of the deprecated helper.

issues.description: Mutable default argument values reference module-level streams at import time
issues.detail: `def redirected(stdout: TextIO = sys.stdout, stderr: TextIO = sys.stderr)` captures whatever `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` were bound to when the module was imported, which is a pre-existing quirk rather than something this PR introduced. Since the function is now deprecated and slated for removal in 5.0, this is informational only — worth noting that the replacement (`contextlib.redirect_stdout`) requires an explicit target and therefore avoids the trap.

dissents.topic: Is deprecating a small, harmless helper worth the user-facing churn?

positions.position: The helper is tiny and stable; deprecating it forces every downstream test suite that imports it to either silence the warning or migrate. The maintenance saving is near zero. A 'soft' note in the docs recommending contextlib would achieve the same education with less downstream noise.

Keeping a redundant wrapper around two stdlib context managers is incidental complexity in the public surface. A clean 4.3 deprecation -> 5.0 removal is the right time to shed it, and the deprecation warning is the standard mechanism users expect from Falcon.

dissents.topic: Should the deprecation message instruct users on the dual-stream replacement?

positions.position: The current message is short and accurate; users can read the linked stdlib docs. Don't bloat the warning text.

`redirected(stdout=a, stderr=b)` in one `with` block doesn't map 1:1 to a single contextlib call. The deprecation note (warning or docstring) should show the `with redirect_stdout(a), redirect_stderr(b):` form so users don't bounce off the migration.
